definition: One of two or more compounds with the same atoms joined in the same order by the same types of bond, but arranged differently in space.

Stereoisomerism caused by restricted rotation about a C=C bond or within a ring, when each of the two carbons involved carries two different groups: the cis isomer has the matching groups on the same side, the trans isomer on opposite sides.
A carbon atom with four different atoms or groups attached; a molecule with one such carbon cannot be superimposed on its mirror image.
One of a pair of stereoisomers that are mirror images of each other and cannot be superimposed.
The ability of a substance to rotate the plane of plane-polarized light; under the same conditions, two enantiomers rotate it by the same angle in opposite directions.
